candidate_findings.title: Destructive cleanup lacks committed-work reachability guards
candidate_findings.gap: Removal confirmation and blocking are keyed to dirty state and active runs, the cleanup default may silently remove a clean worktree, and the destructive dirty path force-deletes the branch. No state is specified for unmerged commits, unpushed commits, open PRs, or whether the branch is the last named reference to committed work.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A clean worktree can still contain unique committed work, and a dirty worktree can contain both unique commits and uncommitted changes. Pruning plus branch deletion can remove the user's only obvious recovery reference without the stated safeguards detecting that risk.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The committed-work safety oracle for remove and delete is absent: merged/reachable/ahead/pushed/PR states and the corresponding block, preserve, or destructive outcomes are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Create and bind persistence has no crash-consistency contract
candidate_findings.gap: A successful create spans a Git filesystem mutation, a worktree record write, a thread-binding write, and a seglog event, while binding reconstruction later treats events as authoritative and startup repair only describes a missing-path case. The capsule does not define transaction boundaries, ordering authority, rollback, or reconciliation for partial success.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash can leave a real worktree without complete records, a binding without its event or reverse lookup, or an event whose durable record is missing. Replay and redb can then disagree about ownership and 1:1 binding.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The precedence rules and recovery transitions for every partial-write combination across Git, redb, reverse lookup, and seglog are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: The fetch step does not establish the stated local-target freshness
candidate_findings.gap: The target is explicitly an existing local branch, but the only freshness step is `git fetch origin {target_branch}` followed by operations against the local target. No step updates the local target from the fetched ref or pins the merge and test inputs to a fetched SHA, and an offline fetch failure is allowed to proceed.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The merge can be tested and completed against a stale local target while the UI contract says the fetch makes that target up to date.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The exact target ref or commit used after fetch, the local-versus-remote synchronization rule, and the freshness status shown when local-only execution proceeds are not defined.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Must be existing local branch
Before any merge strategy, the backend runs `git fetch origin {target_branch}` in the main repo so the local target is up-to-date.

candidate_findings.title: Age-only stale-lock cleanup can unlock a live merge
candidate_findings.gap: The lock covers the entire rebase, test, and fast-forward sequence, and the configured test timeout alone is five minutes, yet startup removes a lock when its age exceeds five minutes even if its PID is still alive because the rule uses `PID dead or lock older than 5 minutes`.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A second process or startup recovery path can admit another merge while the first operation is legitimately still running, enabling concurrent mutation of the main repository and worktree.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Live-owner identity, lease renewal or heartbeat semantics, PID-reuse handling, and a safe takeover condition for long-running operations are absent.

evidence_refs.excerpt: `300` | "Pre-merge test timeout (seconds)" | Abort test run if it exceeds this duration
For Rebase, the lock covers the ENTIRE sequence from worktree rebase through tests to main repo ff-merge.
if PID dead or lock older than 5 minutes → auto-remove.

candidate_findings.title: Cancel and non-rebase failure rollback are undefined
candidate_findings.gap: Cancel remains enabled after merge mutation begins, hook failures expose Retry or Cancel, but only rebase conflicts have an explicit abort and lock-release transition. The capsule does not define what Cancel does to a running Git process or how squash/merge conflicts, failed checkout or commit, staged changes, hook-modified files, and the merge lock are reconciled.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The main repository can remain on another branch, with an in-progress merge or modified index and working tree, while the UI returns to an apparently retryable state.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: A phase-specific cancel/failure state machine, repository postconditions, rollback boundaries, lock-release rules, and retry preconditions are missing for every mutation phase other than the cited rebase-conflict case.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Cancel remains enabled for user abort.

Hook failure = merge failure with Retry/Cancel. Standard commit hooks run at their normal Git trigger points during the merge/commit step after any pre-merge test passes; `pre-merge-commit` runs during `git merge --no-ff` commit and gets the same treatment as pre-commit failure. For `prepare-commit-msg`, PM's provided commit message is the initial value; hooks may append/modify it before the commit is finalized. If hooks modify files, for example auto-formatting in a pre-commit hook, the test gate tests the PRE-hook state; hooks run after test pass as part of the commit pipeline, not the test pipeline.
Auto-abort (`git rebase --abort`). Dialog shows error. Tests never run. Lock released.

candidate_findings.title: User-controlled Git arguments lack a process-invocation safety contract
candidate_findings.gap: The commit message is editable and multi-line, while command templates interpolate `{branch}`, `{target}`, and `"{message}"`. The capsule does not state whether Git is invoked with an argument vector, how quotes and newlines are encoded, or which ref validation is applied at execution time.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A shell-based or string-tokenized implementation can misparse user content, execute unintended arguments or commands, or target the wrong ref.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The process-boundary contract for literal argument passing, option termination, commit-message transport, and execution-time ref validation is absent.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Commit message | Text area (multi-line) | Auto-generated per strategy | Editable
`git checkout {target}` → `git merge --no-ff {branch} -m "{message}"`

candidate_findings.title: PR panel chronology conflates opening and submission
candidate_findings.gap: The flow says it opens a pre-filled PR panel, then says push occurs before the panel opens, and further says an API failure after push means the panel does not open. It never identifies when the user reviews or edits the fields, when the API call is initiated, or what panel state survives a failed submission.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The UI can perform a remote side effect before the user sees the form, then hide the editable recovery surface after failure, making status and retry behavior misleading.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The ordered states for panel open, field review, push, API submit, failure recovery, and preservation of user edits are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Create Anyway branch-collision behavior lacks executable semantics
candidate_findings.gap: An existing branch is treated as an advisory-only condition and `Create Anyway` promises to proceed, but the capsule does not distinguish a branch merely existing from it already being checked out in another worktree, nor define rejection, forced checkout, or shared-ref behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The action can be impossible under normal Git constraints or can create branch-level interference that the worktree-id 1:1 rule does not prevent.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Collision states and their observable outcomes, including checked-out-elsewhere, stale branch, and concurrent branch ownership, are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: The main-repository dirty guard is narrower than the mutation surface
candidate_findings.gap: Main-repository dirtiness blocks only the squash/merge plus `merged_result` combination, although merge execution occurs in the main working tree and Rebase also checks out the target and fast-forwards there. Behavior is not specified for dirty main state when tests are disabled, `branch_only` is selected, or Rebase is used.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Uncommitted main-repository changes can prevent checkout, carry across branches, contaminate the merge context, or be stranded by a partial operation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The dirty-main guard and failure postconditions are missing for the complete strategy-by-test-mode matrix.

candidate_findings.title: The merged-result test oracle excludes hook-modified final content
candidate_findings.gap: The setting claims to test the integrated result and block merge on failure, but hooks run after that test and may modify files before the commit is finalized. No re-test or tree-identity comparison is specified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The committed result can differ from the exact tree that passed the gate, so a green pre-merge result is not an oracle for the delivered merge.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The authoritative tested tree or commit identity, treatment of hook-induced changes, and pass/fail status when final content differs from tested content are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Startup revalidation does not prove recorded worktree identity
candidate_findings.gap: Startup only verifies that the recorded path exists and appears in `git worktree list`, while turn dispatch freezes the stored worktree identity and working directory. It does not state that the listed entry must match the recorded repo, worktree id, branch, or expected HEAD.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A deleted and later reused path, stale record, or mismatched Git entry can pass the stated check and cause a turn to execute against a different worktree than the binding claims.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The identity-match predicate and mismatch transitions for repo, path, worktree id, branch, and HEAD are absent.

candidate_findings.title: PR remote selection hardcodes origin despite a generic GitHub-remote guard
candidate_findings.gap: The push command always targets `origin`, while the only guard requires a configured GitHub remote and does not say that the configured remote must be named `origin` or map to it.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Repositories using a custom remote name or fork/upstream topology can fail or push the branch to the wrong server, which is both a compatibility and unintended-disclosure risk.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The authoritative remote-selection rule, validation that the selected remote is the configured GitHub endpoint, and behavior for multiple remotes are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: ACD-424 has no runtime oracle for its user-visible capability states
candidate_findings.gap: The requirement promises visible unsupported, clamped, gated, unverified, and fallback outcomes, but its only named validation surfaces are the plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators. No behavioral fixture, transition matrix, or rendered/dispatch oracle is identified in the capsule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Plan-governance validation can succeed while Chat renders the wrong capability state, fails to update after owner-schema changes, or dispatches through a route that the UI presents as blocked.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Executable or fixture-based expected outcomes for provider/account/model/effort/media state combinations and their transitions are absent.
